name: Agenda
tagline: A date-focused note taking app for Mac and iOS that ties notes to calendar events and projects.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The concept is simple enough that an agent can nail it in a sitting: notes with dates, notes grouped into projects, a subset pinned as "on the agenda", markdown body, search. What you cannot one-shot is the part people actually love, which is a fast native Mac and iOS editor with real keyboard handling, a sane sync engine, and calendar and reminders integration that does not lose data. A local web app gets you the filing system and none of the muscle memory. If you live in one place on one machine and take notes in markdown anyway, the DIY version is genuinely fine. If you bounce between phone and laptop mid-meeting, you will miss the real thing within a week.
coreLoopDIY: A local app where every note carries a date and a project, some are flagged "on the agenda", and you can import calendar events from an .ics file to attach notes to them.
requirements: optional .ics export from your calendar for event linking
whatYouLose: Polished native Mac and iOS editors, including the fast inline markdown typing experience
Real cross-device sync with conflict handling instead of one SQLite file on one machine
Live two-way calendar and reminders integration rather than a static .ics import
Share and export formats, printing, and the collaboration-adjacent bits
Years of small interaction decisions you would only notice after rebuilding them badly
moatNotes: The data model is a weekend. The typing feel and the sync layer are the product.
whyPeopleStillPay: Note taking apps are judged in milliseconds. People pay because the editor never stutters, the date and project structure is already thought through, and the same note appears on their phone before they have closed the laptop. A homegrown version can copy the schema exactly and still feel like homework, because the value is concentrated in native app craft and in sync you do not have to think about.
notes: Rebuild the filing system in an afternoon, then spend three months failing to rebuild the typing feel.
prompt:
Build a local-first, date-focused note taking app called "Docket". Single machine, single user, no accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Vite + React + TypeScript for the UI
- Express server in the same repo, port 4400
- better-sqlite3 with a single docket.db file in ./data
- Tailwind for styling
- One npm script "dev" that runs server and client together

Data model:
- projects: id, name, archived flag, sort order
- notes: id, project_id, title, body (markdown), note_date (ISO date, required), on_agenda (bool), pinned_event_id nullable, created_at, updated_at
- events: id, ics_uid, title, starts_at, ends_at (imported only, never edited)

Features in scope:
- Three-pane layout: project sidebar, note list, editor
- Every note requires a date; default to today, editable with a date picker
- "On the Agenda" smart view listing every flagged note across all projects, sorted by note_date
- "Today" and "Last 7 days" smart views
- Markdown editor with a plain textarea plus live preview toggle. Support #tags parsed out of the body into a clickable tag filter
- Full text search across title and body using SQLite FTS5
- Import a .ics file from disk: parse VEVENTs, upsert into events, let a note be attached to one event, show event title and time above the note
- Export: dump any project as a folder of .md files with YAML front matter (date, project, tags, on_agenda)
- Keyboard shortcuts: cmd+n new note, cmd+k search, cmd+enter toggle on_agenda

Explicitly out of scope: mobile apps, sync, sharing, real-time collaboration, live calendar APIs, rich text, attachments, auth.

Secrets: none needed. If you add any config, use .env with a committed .env.example.

Deliver a README with setup in under five commands, seed the db with two projects and six sample notes, and make sure the app opens straight into the On the Agenda view.
